content.rationale: The remove verb: with no id (ouyrkmlr) it refuses; an argument the form does not name — a flag, or a second id — refuses, named (RM1); an id that maps to neither a valid node nor the root refuses, naming it (D21, tsspuwzo, xtmprysl) — the read is what decides — and removing nothing (qyynqqpx); an id that names no change — the root, the one id that resolves yet owns none, every other such id being D21's — refuses, naming it (RM4); otherwise it abandons the named node's change only when nothing depends on it (D14, stnqmzuw; D7, myprwuxt) — a dependant refuses the invocation, each named (wnxsoknq, zvtktmpz), an unreadable node refuses it, named (RM3), and a gate that evaluates the named node among others refuses it, named (RM2), while the node's own gates are abandoned with it (D7) — the happy path being zrvnlzvw's, bracketed through M-markers-capture (okkvnnvm) — the lifecycle table's removal case (S5-lifecycle, vwlrqoxk) — with changes abandoned through M-jj-abandon (urtkpxwv), S3-abandon's (xllzxxvo) mechanism, the node set scanned through M-node-set (nykqvuqr), and a successful removal writing nothing (O7-remove, loxpnryv). It resolves the id through M-node-resolve (wynwwtur, hence M-node-load), names the file through M-store-path (vkztyrzm), reads through M-store-read across the runner (M-jj), builds its refusals through M-refusal (popowxnw), takes the injected context (M-context zttrwlts, M-context-injection ryuswoxz), and returns its lines for the envelope to write (M-output-return, utrzvyyt) under M-route's handler shape (ynvwvzrm), carrying its own --help text (xlvoxmyl/rwlywqrk, per oqnsuzqu). I1-serde (orrvsxqq) fixes the JSON layer the module is written against — serde and serde_json, the crate's own `Value` and the derive. It hands the store to the capture bracket through the context's fallible accessor (S3-root-required). The read's refusal site (S2-read-refusal-site, vollyzvn) is this invocation's: an unreadable node refuses before anything is abandoned, naming it.
